videos.title: How business leaders budget for generative AI
videos.focus: Budgeting for AI cost categories, capability investment and measurable business value
videos.summary: IBM researcher Anthony Marshall separates generative-AI spending that solves existing problems from investment in new capabilities. The lesson covers major cost buckets, common budgeting errors and research-backed practices used by stronger-performing organizations.
videos.why_it_matters: Leaders can turn a vague AI budget into an explicit portfolio: label operating and capability investments, identify recurring costs, connect each line to an outcome and stop funding pilots that cannot show a decision-useful measure.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed the complete IBM AI Academy episode page, exact runtime, named presenter, learning objectives and substantive companion guidance; final playback proof is delegated to the protected signed-out runner.

quality_review.learning_objective: Separate generative-AI cost categories and connect spending decisions with existing-problem savings or genuinely new organizational capabilities.
quality_review.practical_action: Review one AI budget, label each item as operating cost, existing-problem improvement or new capability, then attach a measurable outcome and review date.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected after YouTube playback could not be proven because this unused publisher-hosted lesson has an exact runtime, full player, clear learning objectives and a bounded budgeting exercise.

transferable_takeaways: Distinguish spending that improves an existing process from investment that creates a new capability.
Track recurring operating costs separately from one-time experimentation and implementation expense.
Require every funded AI initiative to name a measurable outcome, review owner and stop condition.

videos.title: Achieving AI-readiness with hybrid cloud
videos.focus: Connecting data, models and infrastructure through an intentional hybrid-cloud architecture
videos.summary: IBM infrastructure CTO Hillery Hunter explains how fragmented environments make data and models hard to find and reuse. The lesson frames intentional hybrid cloud as an architecture decision for integrating data, AI workloads, operational agility and scalable deployment.
videos.why_it_matters: Teams can use the lesson as an architecture review: locate data and models, identify cross-environment friction, define placement constraints and decide which integration work must happen before scaling an AI workload.

verification.content_review_basis: Reviewed the complete IBM AI Academy episode page, exact runtime, named presenter, learning objectives and substantive companion guidance; final playback proof is delegated to the protected signed-out runner.

quality_review.practical_action: Map one AI workload across data location, model access, compute placement, governance and operations, then flag every handoff that prevents repeatable deployment.
quality_review.selected_over_alternatives: Selected after YouTube playback could not be proven because the unused IBM-hosted episode exposes a full player, exact runtime and a practical architecture-review objective.

complete_compiler_story.summary: AWS shows a complete multi-turn reinforcement-learning pipeline for teaching GPT-OSS-20B to play Wordle on SageMaker AI. complete_compiler_story.headline: IBM keeps interpretability hooks compatible with high-performance vLLM execution
complete_compiler_story.summary: IBM Research introduces vLLM-Hook, a model-internals access layer that preserves vLLM graph replay while supporting activation inspection and steering. In publisher-run experiments, the team reports up to 20× lower instrumentation overhead than its predecessor, with roughly 2% overhead on small models and 6% on a 70-billion-parameter model.
complete_compiler_story.why_it_matters: You will learn where interpretability tooling can distort production inference and how graph-aware hooks reduce that penalty. The reported overhead ranges also provide a practical benchmark for deciding whether observability experiments belong in a serving-path evaluation.

audience_fit.intended_user: A field-service operations leader who manages technician preparation, evidence access, debrief quality and human accountability.
audience_fit.practical_action: Select one recurring service visit and define the pre-visit facts, approved evidence sources, debrief questions and decisions reserved for technicians.
audience_fit.review_action: Compare agent briefs and voice debriefs with completed work orders, then record omissions, unsupported suggestions and technician corrections.
audience_fit.usable_outcome: A bounded field-service pilot with a source checklist, human decision boundary, debrief template and measurable documentation-quality review.

primary_source.title: Data and AI agents give a lift to TK Elevator service technicians

verified_read_evidence.scope: Reviewed the complete Microsoft and TK Elevator feature, 25,000-technician and 1.4-million-unit scope, pre-visit brief, IoT and manual retrieval, mobile access, voice debrief, follow-up questions, human responsibility, vendor-case-study framing and limitations.

visual_specification.original_image_alt_intent: A service technician using a phone beside an elevator, with an agent brief assembling tools, IoT signals, manuals and prior notes before a human-approved repair and voice debrief.
visual_specification.source_faithful_mechanism: Microsoft and TK Elevator describe a mobile AI assistant for 25,000 service technicians maintaining 1.4 million units. Before a visit, it assembles tools, location details and likely issues from IoT data, manuals and notes. Afterward, a voice debrief gathers missing facts, while technicians retain responsibility for diagnosis and action.
visual_specification.explanatory_significance: You will learn how to structure a field-service workflow around pre-visit briefs, evidence retrieval, voice debriefs and human decision authority. The pattern helps operations leaders evaluate assistance that reduces search and documentation work without delegating safety-critical judgment.
visual_specification.factual_scope: Reviewed the complete Microsoft and TK Elevator feature, 25,000-technician and 1.4-million-unit scope, pre-visit brief, IoT and manual retrieval, mobile access, voice debrief, follow-up questions, human responsibility, vendor-case-study framing and limitations.
visual_specification.label_authority: Owner requires explanatory text; app prepares exact wording without claiming separate owner review.
